result.observations:
Summary for preflight: which wait fails first is decided by RTF. At run 03's RTF (about 0.1) the MAVROS 10 s wall timeout (needs RTF >= 0.1) breaks next, then the 3 s sim yaw lock inside 45 s wall (needs >= 0.067). Run 03 sat at or below all of these.

1. The effective MAVROS connection timeout is 10 s wall, not 8 s. MAVROS 2.14 declares 'conn_timeout' (default 10.0) with create_wall_timer, reset on every HEARTBEAT (sys_status.cpp:505-511 and 951; source read from sim/ros_stack/mavros-2.14.0.tar.gz). The 'conn.timeout: 8' in mavros.yaml:9,41 and sim/ros_stack/mavros214.yaml:9 is a ROS1-era name and has no effect. Run 03 confirms it: the disconnect States at 43.1 s and 55.8 s came 10.07 s and 10.03 s after the HEARTBEATs at 33.03 s and 45.77 s. So connected=true needs RTF > 0.1 with zero margin, not 0.125. gate.py:52 already states 10 s.

2. Measured RTF, from proxy px4_sim versus wall over each heartbeat interval:
   - Run 02: 0.44-0.48 during startup, 0.33-0.42 during parameter writes, 0.30-0.36 after OFFBOARD with the detector and pipeline probe running, 0.19-0.27 during revert.
   - Run 03: 0.19 → 0.12 → 0.08-0.10 for the whole run (overall 0.107), with the detector still IDLE.
   - Activating vision plus the probe cost run 02 about 25-45% of its RTF.
   - Computed with /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-arsenij-Documents-Bumbl-code/f507fbf5-623a-4fe8-a0f8-538c2c983db6/scratchpad/rtf_audit/vision_flight/rtf.py.

3. MAVROS disconnects set off a cascade. Below RTF 0.1, MAVROS publishes State(connected=false, armed=false, mode='').
   - aruco_detect (lines 553-583) reads mode and armed from it and goes IDLE, destroying the image subscription. Poses and yaw_locked stop, and the full_rate_when_armed protection does not help in flight.
   - simple_offboard handleState (lines 662/679) treats it as a disarm edge and silently resets the setpoint stream. In flight that ends in a PX4 offboard-loss failsafe.
   - camera_fix.py:74-79 records that recreating a subscription from a timer can corrupt the rclpy wait-set, and aruco does exactly that, so repeated flapping adds risk.

4. Vision throughput (run 02 pipeline.json):
   - /clock arrives at 247.5 Hz sim, one per physics step.
   - The bridge outputs 18.1 Hz sim (4.5 Hz wall), limited by CPU. In run 03 it ran at about 24 Hz sim, limited by sim pace.

result.observations:
## When the error is raised

"proxy guard unavailable or conflicted" has one source: RosRawBridge._status (ros_raw_bridge.py:78-80). It fires when any of these holds:
- **(a)** status.json 'received' is not within 0-0.5 s of the bridge's time.monotonic() (same VM kernel clock as the proxy).
- **(b)** status 'fault' is not null.
- **(c)** writer != [245,190]. The writer is constant, so this never fires.

read_fresh reaches _status only before it publishes:
- every <=20 ms loop pass inside state() (line 145);
- twice inside _request_heartbeat (lines 103, 120);
- once in _send (line 198).

**Transient vs sticky:**
- **(a) is transient.** It means the proxy loop did not complete guard.tick() for >0.5 s wall.
- **(b) is sticky** for the proxy's lifetime. The policy faults are: write_without_disarmed_inhibition, foreign_parameter_writer, unsupported_parameter_protocol, unparsed_outbound, storage_or_reboot_command, invalid_arm_disarm_request, invalid_base_mode.
- After the proxy exits (900 s, or proxy_stop), (a) becomes permanent.

## How it relates to sim speed

- **(a) has no sim-paced refresh.** tick runs at the top of every loop pass, bounded by select(0.02). Its min_rtf is 0.
- **Common cause, not causation.** Low RTF and a stale status are both symptoms of the same VM/host starvation. The 'received' value is stamped before json.dump + fsync, and the loop also writes to the /work virtiofs mount, so I/O stalls age the status directly.
- **The one RTF-coupled sticky path into (b)** is the PARAM_SET heartbeat check (proxy_profile_policy.py:171), which has only 50 ms of headroom. It needs RTF >= 1/(1-L) or path latency L <= 50 ms.

## Run 02

- **RTF from the proxy's px4_sim:** 0.51 at the start, falling to 0.17 at the end.
- **What happened:** revert_all completed (18.97 s) at 53505.053. The old supervisor read_all, which had no retry, failed at 53506.119.
- **Evidence of a VM-wide stall** (an ~0.6 s proxy stall during a near-freeze of the sim):
  - fault stayed null in guard_final/status.json;
  - the proxy wrote no records between 53505.400 and 53506.023;
  - RC emulator and MAVROS sequence numbers are consecutive across the gap;
  - PX4 advanced only 0.048 sim s over 1.48 wall s (RTF about 0.03), while requested-heartbeat replies in 2-6 ms show the proxy had no inbound backlog.
- **Recovery:** cleanup revert and verify succeeded afterwards. The current flight_trial_01 supervisor retries exactly this transient in read_all.
- **The vpe_fix transaction has no such tolerance.** Any RuntimeError there sets the journal to 'unknown', and later restores are refused 'not_ready'.

## Run 03

- RTF was 0.08-0.19. The failure happened in the supervisor before any code in this area ran beyond bridge construction.
- RosRawBridge cannot request a heartbeat before it has seen one (lines 107-108, 151-153). So supervisor.py:164 has to wait for natural heartbeats: min_rtf = 2/15 = 0.133, while the in-window RTF was 0.097.
- The request path is wall-paced (PX4 receiver thread; median 3 ms, max 137 ms in run 02, up to 712 ms in run 03). It is the only heartbeat source that does not depend on RTF, and it runs only during parameter operations in inhibit mode.

## Biggest risks for the next runs

1. **Restore budget.** Restore is one 30 s wall transaction of about 779 MAVLink operations (19 s in run 02). It tolerates nothing: a single 0.5 s proxy stall, one lost PARAM_REQUEST_READ/PARAM_VALUE (no per-request retry), or the zero-headroom _guard race (profile_transaction.py:58) makes the journal 'unknown' and stops any automatic restore. At run-03 load (~0.27 s/read) it cannot finish at all.
2. **Queue overflow.** The supervisor bridge's raw queue overflows (sticky 'raw_queue_overflow') below RTF of about 0.15, because PX4 clamp transients make vpe_fix rescan for 1 sim s per clamped write.
3. **RTF >= 1 in flight mode.** Natural heartbeats at RTF >= 1 are needed for armed RC forwarding in flight mode (proxy_profile_policy.py:122), for OFFBOARD admission in inhibit mode (line 112), and for any state() call in flight mode (ros_raw_bridge.py:104).
4. **PARAM_SET headroom.** The 50 ms PARAM_SET headroom (sticky fault) is RTF-sensitive below 1/(1-L).

## Other points

- **Freshness stamps are processing times.** The bridge stamps the ROS callback time; the proxy stamps its loop processing time. A queued heartbeat therefore looks fresh.
- **Executor capacity.** vpe_fix runs a 2-thread executor. One thread is blocked in the service handler, and the other must decode the full /uas1/mavlink_source stream, whose rate is proportional to RTF. Higher RTF and higher load slow every read.
- **Proxy throughput.** The proxy processes one datagram per socket per pass and does an fsync per pass. Under drops, the FCU sequence check can reject heartbeats. Not seen in runs 02/03.
- **Journal growth.** The journal (563 KB in run 02) is fully rewritten and fsynced after every scan, so low-RTF transients slow every later save.
- **Shared identity.** The observer (supervisor) bridge and the writer (vpe_fix) bridge share the identity (245,190), so the proxy cannot tell them apart.

## Options, not applied (check consequences first)

- **Stamp after fsync.** Stamp 'received' after the fsync, or measure the 0.5 s from the file's mtime. This hides less, but still fails on real stalls.
- **Retry reads, never SETs.** Inside the transaction, retry idempotent reads on a transient stale status or a missing PARAM_VALUE, with a per-request timeout. Never retry a SET blindly: re-verify it by reading back.
- **Add headroom to _guard**, e.g. state(max_age=0.95).
- **Wall-paced heartbeats for supervisor.py:164.** Let it call its own bridge.state() to get wall-paced heartbeats. Consequence: this would also keep MAVROS 'connected' and mask a slow sim, so log the RTF separately.
- **Bound the restore differently.** Give the restore a larger wall budget scaled to measured per-read latency, or split it into per-parameter steps. The journal semantics must be re-reviewed if this is done.
- **Observer queue.** Drain or raise the observer bridge's queue limit, or make overflow non-sticky for read-only observers.

result.observations:
1) Clock model. Every wait in supervisor.py uses time.monotonic (the supervisor node does not set use_sim_time), and so do the run.sh and sitl_setup bounds. The things being waited for are mostly sim-paced: PX4 HEARTBEAT at 1 Hz sim, camera at 30 Hz sim, and param transactions. In the MAVROS 2.14 source, conn_timeout, heartbeat_rate and the param and command timeouts all use wall clocks (create_wall_timer / std::future), while node->now() and the State header stamps use sim time. vpe_fix, simple_offboard, aruco_detect and setpoint_freshness use sim time.

2) Measured RTF, from the proxy log's px4_sim against VM monotonic wall time.
- Run 03 averaged 0.107 over the whole run. In 5 s bins it was 0.08-0.23; during the line 164 window it was 0.079-0.097.
- Run 02 started at 0.51 and fell steadily to about 0.18 (bins: 0.51, 0.46, 0.43, 0.39, …, 0.21, 0.18). Even run 02 was close to the line 133 limit by the end.

3) Correction to the lead's facts: MAVROS conn.timeout is effectively 10 s wall, not 8. The key `conn.timeout: 8` (mavros.yaml:9 and :41, from sim/ros_stack/mavros214.yaml:9) is a ROS1-style key that nothing in MAVROS 2.14 reads. The real parameter is /mavros/sys conn_timeout (MV/sys_status.cpp:505, default 10.0, wall timer). start_mavros.py / mavros_scoped_config.py never write a /mavros/sys section. Run 03 timing confirms 10 s:
- a 9.59 s HB gap did not disconnect;
- the disconnects came +10.07 s and +10.03 s after the last HB;
- gate.py:52/217/367 already records actual_mavros_conn_timeout_wall=10.

sys_time is not in plugin_allowlist, so there is no TIMESYNC or SYSTEM_TIME (nothing timesync-related depends on RTF). heartbeat_rate and command_ack_timeout are at their defaults (1 Hz wall, 5 s wall).

4) Preflight minimum RTF, worst case, strictest first:
- revert_all against its 30 s server deadline: about 0.17. This is an estimate from run 02's 5.10 s sim cost and is likely 0.17-0.2 because HEARTBEAT-refresh stalls grow at low RTF.
- supervisor.py:133, 3 HB in 20 s wall: 0.15.
- supervisor.py:164, 2 HB in 15 s wall: 0.133. This is the one that failed in run 03.
- MAVROS 10 s connection timeout: 0.10. This also gates the single-shot cleanup checks at supervisor.py:228 and 222 (and 203); below RTF 0.1 the cleanup revert or LAND can be skipped silently.
- Lines 140 and 156: 0.067 each. Line 185 (yaw lock): 0.067. Line 183: 0.051. read_all: about 0.053. set_param: 0.044. Everything else is under 0.03 or wall-only.

So preflight needs a sustained RTF of at least about 0.2 (about 0.25 with margin). Run 03 at about 0.1 would have failed at line 164, then line 133, then most likely revert_all. Non-preflight scenarios additionally need 0.133 (gate.py:253 ground-settle window) and 0.45 (gate.py:369 heartbeat scenario).

5) Extra heartbeats. The bridges inject HEARTBEATs on demand using MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE (command 512) from writer 245/190, rate-limited to one per 0.5 s wall. PX4 answers within 0.004-0.016 s sim (run 02) or 0.02-0.084 s sim (run 03). That is why heartbeats arrive at irregular wall times during parameter work: 26.46, 26.87, 28.02 and 29.31 in run 03. These requests are what make reads and writes largely independent of RTF despite the 1.0 s wall HB-freshness rules (ros_raw_bridge.py:134-195; proxy_profile_policy.py:112, 122, 169-172). The pure HB-count waits (supervisor.py:133, 140, 156, 164) get no such help.

6) Load hits both sides at once. The same CPU starvation that lowers RTF also stretches the wall-only steps. In run 03, wrapper start-up used 10.5 of its 20 s (line 163), and proxy status.json staleness over 0.5 s wall killed run 02 at 64.76 s. Run 02 used an older supervisor (sha 30a8c1c3…) that did not have the observer retry now at lines 113-118; the retry was added for run 03 and handles that failure.

7) Cross-area windows worth noting (combined_03, not in this area): the proxy accepts PARAM_SET, inhibit-mode OFFBOARD, and armed-throttle RC only if the last PX4 HEARTBEAT is at most 1.0 s wall old, i.e. a 1/1.0 = 1.0 RTF requirement unless a 512 refresh happened just before. The bridge requires status.json at most 0.5 s old. The vpe_fix server caps transactions at 30 s wall. Wall-paced senders (rc_emulator GCS HB and RC override, MAVROS HB) only become a problem at high RTF (above roughly 2.5), never at low RTF. The PX4 stream rates (RC_CHANNELS 20, SYS_STATUS 5, LOCAL_POSITION_NED 30 Hz sim) and HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT 2.5 s are PX4 defaults from memory and were not checked against on-disk source.

8) Other findings.
- run_sim.snapshot.sh:137-141 never fails on a slow PX4 start; it just continues.
- sitl_setup.py capture_baseline and collect_restoration (with their 30 s windows) are not called from main().
- pipeline_probe's 120 s sim / 700 s wall settings make its pipeline.json incomplete below RTF 0.171. It is diagnostic only.

All read-only; nothing was modified and no Lima VM was touched.

result.diagnosis_reasoning:
VERDICT: confirmed. Line 164 is the failing assert, and the proximate cause is too little PX4/Gazebo time passing in the 15 s wall window. The slowness came from the environment, not the product. Several of the lead's supporting facts need correcting (point 5).

1) Which assert failed.
- The failure is at monotonic 53715.209 (55.33 s after started_wall 53659.874). It is a bare AssertionError, and no service_reply comes before it.
- independent_before was already saved (reads received 53684.53-53689.60), so only line 163 or line 164 can be the failing assert.
- Line 163 would have failed at about spawn+20 s, roughly 53709.6. The wrapper was spawned right after the last read at 53689.60. The actual failure is 25.6 s after that read. So line 163 passed at about 53700.2 and line 164 expired exactly 15.0 s later.
- The wrapper's own timing agrees: rclpy init at about 53696.1-53696.3, 'vpe_fix ready' at about 53698.9-53699.1, first _gate_tick at 53700.227 on the wrapper's own monotonic clock.
- In the window 53700.2-53715.2 the supervisor counted 1 HEARTBEAT (53705.644). The next one arrived at 53715.958, 0.75 s after the deadline.

2) Mechanism.
- PX4 sent HEARTBEATs exactly every 1.000 s of PX4 time (proxy px4_sim 17.184, 18.188, 19.184, 20.184, 21.18, 22.192, 23.188).
- The extra ones at 20.476, 20.516, 20.776 and 20.88 are replies to the supervisor bridge's 4 REQUEST_MESSAGE(512) calls during read_all.
- All 11 PX4 HEARTBEATs were forwarded: no dropped_heartbeat and no sequence rejection. Each reached the supervisor 4-42 ms after the proxy.
- No 512 request was sent after 53689.02. The wrapper bridge cannot request a heartbeat before it has seen one (ros_raw_bridge.py:107-108, 151-153).
- PX4 time advanced 1.38 s during the window (RTF 0.092). Given the phase (the window opened 0.58 s of sim after the 21.18 HEARTBEAT), 1.43 s was needed.

Three independent clocks give the same RTF of about 0.08-0.10:
- proxy px4_sim: 0.079 over 33.03-45.77 s and 0.097 over 45.77-56.08 s;
- ROS /clock as seen by vpe_fix _gate_tick: ROS 21.724, 22.0 and 23.0 s at monotonic 53700.227, 53703.522 and 53714.023, giving 0.084 and 0.095. PX4 time interpolated at 53700.227 is also 21.724, so Gazebo and PX4 time agree;
- the camera bridge: '120 strict frames' is about 24 Hz sim × 5 s of sim in about 46 s wall.

3) Environment or product?
- Before any ROS or product process existed, PX4 startup took 42 one-second loop iterations against 11 in run 02. The ULog logger opened 51 s after run start against 15 s. Yet the lockstep part of rcS was about 1 s of sim in both runs (14.288→15.40 vs 10.464→11.38), so the extra time was wall-paced work.
- RTF over the first HEARTBEAT interval was 0.19, against 0.565 in run 02.
- Wall-paced work was about 10x slower, not just the sim:

| Wall-paced step | Run 03 | Run 02 |
|---|---|---|
| Wrapper Python start to rclpy init | 6.5 s | 0.65 s |
| Wrapper start to 'vpe_fix ready' | 9.3 s | 0.8 s |
| 19 supervisor reads | 5.07 s | 0.16 s |
| REQUEST_MESSAGE to HEARTBEAT reply | 48-712 ms | 2-6 ms |

- The proxy processed the rc_emulator's steady 1 Hz GCS HEARTBEATs (sender max gap 1.058 s) with 0.4-1.1 s jitter.
- VM process lists are identical except for launch temp-file names.
- The guest CLOCK_REALTIME−CLOCK_MONOTONIC offset was constant through run 02 (1792003907.5045 s, ±0.1 ms). It moved by about −3.2 s before run 03 and by a further −0.1 to −0.27 s during run 03.
- Circumstantial: host-side parallel jobs wrote files during run 03 and not during run 02 (field_measurements_01 photo analysis 13:44:43-47, make_aruco_world 13:45:38-40, check_textures 13:48:03).
- The VM has 2 vCPUs. The 2026-10-17 probe measured a ceiling of 0.29 RTF with the GUI on and 0.50 with it paused, running only gz, PX4 and the camera nodes.
- The product does add load: RTF fell from 0.10-0.13 to 0.074 while the vpe_fix wrapper started (run 02: 0.49→0.44). That load was also present in run 02. Even at 0.10-0.13, line 133 (needs ≥0.15) would have failed later, because vision plus pipeline_probe roughly halve RTF in that phase (run 02 fell from 0.38 to 0.17-0.19).

4) Other causes ruled out:
- proxy drops or HEARTBEAT sequence rejection;
- endpoint mismatch (lines 142-144 passed);
- DDS loss;
- supervisor callback starvation: the 23.188 HEARTBEAT was generated after the deadline, since ROS time was 23.0 at 53714.02;
- a product refusal: no service was called before the failure.

5) Corrections to the lead's facts:
- 'sensor_gyro lost' is also in run 02 (generation 70→115), so it does not distinguish run 03.
- The MAVROS connection timeout is effectively 10 s wall. 'conn.timeout: 8' is ignored; the sys plugin is a separate node /mavros/sys (plugin.hpp:82-87) with default conn_timeout 10 (sys_status.cpp:505-511). Run 03 disconnects came 10.07 s and 10.03 s after the last HEARTBEAT, and a 9.57 s gap did not disconnect.
- 'vpe_fix ready' was at about 39.0-39.2 s, not 38.4 s. Run 03's epoch↔monotonic offset was not constant, so one fixed offset gives the wrong time.

6) If line 164 had passed, run 03 would almost certainly have failed next. revert_all at this load needs about 779 operations at 0.27 s per read, roughly 200 s against a 30 s deadline. Line 133 needs ≥0.15.

result.measurement_method:
PRIMARY CLOCK: PX4 time from the MAVLink stream the supervisor already decodes.
- In observe() (supervisor.py:64-78), for each 1/1 message of type ATTITUDE, ATTITUDE_QUATERNION, LOCAL_POSITION_NED, GLOBAL_POSITION_INT or SYSTEM_TIME (the same set the proxy uses, mavlink_fault_proxy_profile.py:54-55), set px4 = max(px4, time_boot_ms/1000).
- Append (time.monotonic(), px4) to a ring buffer at no more than 10 Hz, and save it in flight_result.json.
- Why this clock: HEARTBEATs are scheduled by PX4's own clock, so this is exactly the quantity the heartbeat-count waits depend on. It arrives on the same /uas1/mavlink_source path as the heartbeats, with no new subscription. In run 03 it matched ROS /clock to about 0.01 s (21.724 at monotonic 53700.227).
- Use monotonic stamps only. Run 03's epoch↔monotonic offset was not constant.

WINDOWS:
- Diagnostic profile: RTF over 5 s windows.
- Validity gate: minimum over the guarded phase (from line 140 to the end of cleanup) of the 10 s sliding-window RTF must be at least 0.20. Then any 15 s window holds at least 2.0 s sim (line 164), any 20 s window at least 4.0 s sim (line 133 needs 3.0), and every HEARTBEAT gap stays under 10 s wall (MAVROS).
- If the gate fails, the run is INVALID (environment) whatever its outcome. Low RTF also hides wall stalls from sim-time freshness checks, so a pass at low RTF proves nothing.

PER-WAIT ACCOUNTING (authoritative for classifying a failure):
- Log PX4 time and heartbeat count at the start and end of each sim-paced wait: lines 140, 156, 164, 183, 184, 185 and 133.
- A failed wait is INVALID (environment) if PX4 time never reached the next required heartbeat slot: last heartbeat sim time + k, with k = 2 for line 164 and 3 for line 133. More simply: sim advance below 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 1.12, 3.25 and 3.0 s respectively.
- Run 03 line 164 qualifies: the slot at 23.188 was reached 0.74 s after the deadline.

STALLS:
- Count wall intervals with no advance of PX4 time as RTF 0. Do not exclude them; a stall is exactly what breaks the waits.
- Tell stalls apart with two cross-checks:
  1. proxy_clock.json: proxy-side px4_sim with proxy monotonic, written at most at 10 Hz, independent of MAVROS and DDS;
  2. /clock: Gazebo time via gz_camera_bridge, the only ROS clock source.
- If Gazebo and the proxy advance but the supervisor's MAVLink-derived time does not, the delivery path failed (MAVROS/DDS/supervisor). That is not low RTF.
- If no MAVLink arrives at all, it is a transport failure.
- If every clock stops, the simulator stalled: INVALID.

WALL-STARVATION MONITOR (needed in addition to RTF, because revert_all, read_all, the status.json 0.5 s check and the PARAM_SET headroom are load-bound). Sample in a supervisor thread:
- status.json age every 50 ms (maximum);
- REQUEST_MESSAGE→HEARTBEAT latency;
- /proc/pressure/cpu and /proc/pressure/io avg10, and loadavg;
- a fixed-work CPU canary (wall time of a constant busy loop, compared with an idle baseline).
Reference points: run 03 showed 512 replies of 48-712 ms against 2-6 ms in run 02, and wrapper start 9.3 s against 0.8 s. Calibrate thresholds from good runs.

EARLY ABORT: measure 10 s RTF right after line 140, before any write. In run 02 the vision-active phase ran at about 0.37× the initial RTF, so an initial RTF below about 0.5 predicts falling under 0.2 at line 133. Run 03 started at 0.146 and should have been stopped as INVALID before the profile was applied.
result.other_risks:
1) Low-RTF passes are not meaningful. A wall stall of G s is G·r s in sim. Sim-time freshness checks become lenient:
- setpoint_freshness MAX_AGE 0.5 s sim;
- vpe_fix _POSE_TIMEOUT 0.5 s sim;
- simple_offboard state_timeout 3 s sim;
- PX4 COM_OF_LOSS_T 1 s sim.
Wall-paced senders (simple_offboard 30 Hz, MAVROS heartbeat 1 Hz, rc_emulator) also deliver 1/r more messages per sim second. A product with multi-second stalls can therefore pass at r=0.1. Low-RTF runs must be INVALID, not PASS.

2) Harness defects that turn slowness into an apparent product failure:
- Bare asserts (supervisor.py:141, 144, 145, 156, 163, 164, 165, 171, 188). Run 03 could only be classified by reconstructing timing.
- The observer PARAM_VALUE queue overflow (ros_raw_bridge.py:24, 67-68) is sticky and not retried. At run 02 scan speed it overflows at r ≤ 0.13-0.16, and at higher r on a faster host. Fix: drain or bound the observer queue. That is not a criteria change.
- Line 133 (strictest, 0.15) runs while pipeline_probe (harness diagnostics, supervisor.py:178) and the Gazebo GUI are still loading the VM. viewer_attach.sh itself says the GUI costs about 180% CPU. On this 2-vCPU VM the 2026-10-17 probe gave 0.29 RTF with the GUI on and 0.50 with it paused. Use the MEASURING flag, stop pipeline_probe after line 185, and/or add vCPUs.
- Single-shot connected checks (lines 203, 222, 228) can silently skip cleanup.

3) Load-bound limits with no RTF signature (need the wall-starvation metric):
- the vpe_fix 30 s transactions (revert_all about 779 operations; run 02 used 63% of the budget; run 03 load implies about 200 s);
- no retry of the 0.5 s status.json check inside vpe_fix (journal becomes 'unknown');
- the 50 ms PARAM_SET headroom, which sets a sticky proxy fault;
- the zero-headroom heartbeat-age re-check in _guard (profile_transaction.py:58 against ros_raw_bridge.py:173). This last one is a product race that also exists at RTF 1 on real hardware with 1 Hz heartbeats.

4) Run 03 was starved for wall-paced work too, not only sim:
- wrapper start 9.3 s against 0.8 s;
- 19 reads 5.07 s against 0.16 s;
- the proxy handled the rc_emulator's regular heartbeats with 0.4-1.1 s jitter;
- the guest realtime/monotonic offset stepped about −3.2 s between runs and drifted about −0.1 to −0.27 s within run 03.
The proxy design (one recvfrom per socket per pass, an fsync per pass, a flush to virtiofs per record) adds latency under load. Its px4_sim and wall stamps are processing times.
